equity_bridge.note: ABF.L_HalfYear_2026.txt:830; charged once here, flows are consolidated

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: Primark new-space contribution of 4-5%/yr (management, FY2026 and medium term) on c. 49% of revenue, with Food c. 1-2% and Sugar flat, blends to c. 3% group revenue growth in FY2027-30; below the 4.6% 3-year revenue CAGR, which was inflated by FY2022-23 input-cost pass-through, and well below the EPS CAGRs, which run from the FY2020-21 pandemic trough
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-1.1% 3yr, 3.4% 5yr) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (4.6%/6.9%) and EPS (16.9%/19.7%). Causes: GBP1.6bn of buybacks FY2023-25 shrank book while EPS rose; EPS 5yr runs from the FY2020 COVID trough (Primark stores shut). Neither series is a usable growth anchor; the base path is built bottom-up from the Primark space-growth guidance instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - lease principal - lease interest (lease interest FY2024-25 GBP102m from note 10; FY2020-23 estimated at GBP90-95m from finance expense less bank interest): FY2020 781, FY2021 389, FY2022 -46, FY2023 160, FY2024 1,209, FY2025 526 (GBPm). 3yr owner-FCF CAGR is undefined (FY2022 base negative); 5yr is -7.6% against -2.5% reported, the gap being the IFRS-16 lease cost that reported FCF omits. The series is dominated by working-capital swings (FY2024 +GBP500m inflow) and the capex step-up from c. GBP0.6bn (FY2020-21) to c. GBP1.2bn (FY2023-25): capex now runs c. 1.9x D&A ex-ROU, which is why the owner-FCF margin (2.7% FY2025) sits far below the 7.6% reported operating margin.

scenario_narratives.base: ABF is two businesses in one share: Primark (c. 49% of revenue, c. 60% of segment profit) and a food portfolio whose branded half (Twinings, Ovaltine, AB Mauri) is steady and whose commodity half (Sugar, Agriculture) is in a trough. The base case takes management's FY2026 guidance at face value (group profit below FY2025, Primark margin c. 10%, Sugar a full-year loss), then lets Primark's 4-5% space growth do the work on revenue while the margin recovers to 13.7% EBITDA by FY2030 as Primark returns to c. 11% and Sugar reaches a mid-cycle c. GBP100m, not the FY2024 peak. The demerger costs c. GBP75m one-off and c. GBP45m/yr thereafter and is otherwise neutral to the flows. The binding constraint on value is capital intensity: capex at 5-6% of revenue against D&A ex-ROU of 3.3-3.7% plus a 2.4% lease charge leaves an owner-FCF margin of only c. 2.5% rising to c. 4%, which is why the house value sits below the price despite a c. 10x P/E.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Primark relaunch works: LFL turns positive in the UK and then Europe, the US (38 stores, nine leases signed) and Gulf franchise accelerate space growth to 5%, and margin returns to 12% as the marketing/digital spend annualises. European sugar prices normalise from 2027, restructuring and lower beet costs add c. GBP70m, and the Tanzania mill contributes, taking Sugar to c. GBP150m. Grocery international brands and Ingredients bolt-ons grow mid-single digit. Group EBITDA margin reaches 14.8% and the demerger, completed in 2027, lets a standalone Primark be valued as a growth retailer; the model credits that only through a 16x terminal cap.
scenario_narratives.bear: Sugar is structural, not cyclical: European oversupply persists, Sugar stays loss-making through FY2027 and never earns more than breakeven, and the Vivergo closure shows policy risk compounding commodity risk. Primark's Europe LFL (-5.6% in H1 2026) does not recover against Shein and Zara's omnichannel reach, so new space is diluted by cannibalisation and rent de-leverages; the margin is stuck at 9.5-10% with investment spend continuing. Grocery US oils and UK bread keep eroding, the Middle East conflict lifts input costs, and all five segments' guidance keeps being cut as it was in April 2026. The demerger still happens, adding cost without a re-rating, and the committed store rollout keeps capex at 5.5% of revenue on a 12.5% EBITDA margin.

valuation_philosophy.summary: House owner-FCF basis with Primark's leases charged as an operating cost, SBC expensed (immaterial at 0.1% of revenue), the share count held flat, NCI deducted once at book, and the GBP1.6bn pension surplus excluded symmetrically with its income. Risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate, which is 8.5% in all three cases. The valuation is deliberately consolidated rather than sum-of-the-parts: the demerger changes who owns the flows, not the flows, and segment data is too thin (FY2023 and FY2025 only) to project five businesses. SOTP memo, for scale and NOT a house number: FY2025 segment adjusted operating profit at street-style EV/EBIT multiples (Primark 1,126 x 12, Grocery 478 x 12, Ingredients 257 x 12, Sugar mid-cycle 100 x 8, Agriculture 25 x 8, central costs and dis-synergies -155 x 10) gives c. GBP21.8bn EV; less lease liabilities 3.0bn and NCI gives c. GBP18.6bn or c. 2,630p/share. The gap between that and the house weighted value is the price of the re-rating thesis, stated rather than buried in the terminal assumption. Sugar is normalised to mid-cycle, not extrapolated from either the FY2024 peak (GBP213m) or the FY2026 trough.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capital intensity: capex at c. 1.9x D&A ex-ROU in FY2025; if the 'multi-year projects completing in 2026' do not bring capex down toward 5% of revenue, owner FCF stays near 2.5% of revenue and the base value falls materially
Sugar: the base assumes a recovery to c. GBP100m by FY2029; every GBP50m of permanent shortfall is roughly GBP0.6bn of EV (c. 85p/share) at the terminal multiple
Primark Europe LFL: space growth of 4-5% is the entire revenue engine; persistent negative LFL both dilutes it and de-leverages the GBP450m/yr lease cost

Lease treatment: charging the GBP453m lease cash cost in the flows is the house convention; a reader using street EV/EBITDA on post-IFRS-16 EBITDA against ex-lease net debt will see a far cheaper stock than this model does
Demerger execution: GBP75m one-off and GBP45m/yr dis-synergies are modelled; a delay past 2027, adverse tax clearance, or a dividend-demerger structure that forces index selling is not
FY2026 results (due c. November 2026) and the July 2026 Q3 trading update are not in the folder; Y1 is built from April 2026 guidance
Pension surplus (GBP1.6bn, c. 168p/share net of the 25% surplus charge) is excluded; any route to extraction is upside not in the numbers
FX: sterling strength is a translation headwind to roughly half the revenue base and a transaction cost on Primark's USD sourcing

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (GBp, regular close); 52-week range 1729.45-2359.0
data_sources.financials: ABF.L_Metrics.csv / core_metrics (FY2018-FY2025 annual, H1 2025, H1 2026) from the extracted Annual Reports FY2019-FY2025 and the H1 2026 Interim Results Announcement (24 weeks to 28 February 2026); lease interest from FY2025 note 10; ROU depreciation from the FY2025 adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation; segment profit FY2023/FY2025 from kpis
data_sources.qualitative: ABF.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-04); ABF.L_Presentation_FY2026.txt (21 April 2026 'Outcome of review of Group structure' and H1 2026 results deck: full-year outlook by segment, demerger costs and timetable)

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report consolidated cash flow statement, 'Share-based payment expense' GBP18m (ABF.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:10509); equity-award taxes nil (no net-share-settlement withholding disclosed); FY2024 GBP31m, FY2023 GBP18m
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in PENCE (GBp = GBX = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 converts the GBP-per-share model value to the pence quote, so intrinsic_value / weighted_iv / entry_price are in pence and comparable to current_price; the *_gbp twins hold the pounds figures. No market FX rate is involved; parity is arithmetic (1826p = GBP 18.26). quote_currency is spelt GBX rather than the house GBp because dcf_engine.py upper-cases both codes before comparing them (GBp -> GBP == GBP) and then skips the conversion entirely, leaving a GBP headline labelled as pence (built 2026-10-04 at 17.13 'GBp' against an 1826p price, -99% upside). GBX is the LSE's own pence code and canonical_iv.py aliases it to the pence family. Switch to GBp once the engine distinguishes the two.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: mid-September, 52/53 weeks (FY2025 = 52 weeks to 13 September 2025; FY2026 ended c. 12 September 2026 and is unreported as at the valuation date)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T15:35:24Z regular close (Friday; LSE), Yahoo Finance chart API; 52-week range 1729.45-2359.0 GBp
inputs.share_count_basis: ~706m ordinary shares at 28 February 2026, estimated from the H1 2026 weighted average of 710m (ABF.L_HalfYear_2026.txt:501) less the shares bought in H1 2026 (GBP128m at c. GBP20.5 = c. 6m) accruing through the period. Interim states no material difference between basic and diluted. Held FLAT: SBC (0.1% of revenue) is expensed in the flows. The remaining GBP117m of the GBP250m buyback (to complete in H2 FY2026) is not pre-credited: the cash funding it is still inside the 28-Feb balance sheet, so count and cash are consistent as at that date.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Financial net debt only: loans and overdrafts GBP709m less cash and cash equivalents GBP712m at 28 February 2026 (ABF.L_HalfYear_2026.txt:1134-1139) = GBP3m net CASH (recorded as net_debt -3). Lease liabilities of GBP3,030m are EXCLUDED because the full lease cash cost is charged inside the flows (treatment B). Company-defined 'total net debt' incl. leases is GBP3,027m (1.2x adjusted EBITDA). Seasonality: the February balance sheet is the cash trough; the September year-end carried GBP390m net cash in FY2025 and GBP1,044m in FY2024.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. Lease principal (FY2025 GBP351m, financing activities, ABF.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:10537) PLUS lease interest (FY2025 GBP102m, note 10 'Interest expense relating to lease liabilities', :12070) are deducted inside adjusted EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path (453/19,459 = 2.33%; H1 2026 174+49 = 223 on 9,470 = 2.35%). Lease liabilities are therefore excluded from net debt. D&A for the cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation: FY2025 adjusted-EBITDA D&A GBP951m (893 depreciation + 58 amortisation of operating intangibles) less GBP305m ROU depreciation (:11498) = GBP646m = 3.3% of revenue. Reported EBITDA margin (13.8% FY2025) is the post-IFRS-16 figure, so the lease deduction sits below it rather than being double-counted in a pre-IFRS-16 margin.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge: non-controlling interests of GBP158m at 28 February 2026 (ABF.L_HalfYear_2026.txt:830) deducted at book via equity_bridge. NCI profit share is GBP20m/yr (c. 2% of attributable profit), so book is a fair proxy. Flows are therefore modelled on a consolidated basis.
inputs.interest_income_treatment: Finance income (FY2025 GBP47m) and other financial income (pension net interest GBP47m) sit BELOW adjusted operating profit, so the EBITDA-based component build never contains them; reported FCF (OCF 2,231 less capex 1,234) is also pre-interest because ABF books interest paid/received outside operating activities. interest_income is set to 0 in the owner-FCF deduction for that reason, and net cash (GBP3m) is immaterial against the flows, so nothing is counted twice.
inputs.owner_fcf_bridge_fy2025: reported_fcf 997 - sbc 18 - lease principal 351 - lease interest 102 = 526 (2.7% of revenue). Component cross-check FY2025: adj EBITDA 2,685 - SBC 18 - lease 453 - D&A ex-ROU 646 = EBIT 1,568; cash tax paid 298 -> 1,270; + D&A 646 - capex 1,234 - working-capital outflow c. 150 = c. 530. Ties within noise.
inputs.pension_surplus_note: Net pension asset GBP1,567m at FY2025 (funded scheme surplus GBP1,586m, ABF.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:15014) is deliberately NOT in the equity bridge: surplus extraction needs trustee agreement and bears a 25% authorised-surplus charge, and the group has no cash contribution obligation that the flows are relieved of. Memo only: 1,586 x 0.75 / 706 = c. 168p/share of potential value if ever released. Its income (GBP47m other financial income) is equally excluded from the flows, so the exclusion is symmetric.
inputs.wacc_rationale: GBP flows, GBP-built rate: 10-year gilt c. 4.5%, equity risk premium 5.0%, beta c. 0.9 (low-beta consumer staples/value retail blend) -> cost of equity c. 9.0%; after-tax cost of debt c. 4%; financial debt ex-leases is <5% of capital -> WACC c. 8.5%. Identical across scenarios: cyclicality (Sugar, Primark LFL) is charged in the flows and the weights, not in the rate. Lease cost is in the flows, so the lease book does not enter the capital structure weighting.
inputs.demerger_treatment: Board decided 21 April 2026 to demerge Primark from the Food businesses (FoodCo) by dividend demerger, targeted before end-calendar-2027, subject to approvals and tax clearances; Wittington (majority holder) supportive. Modelled on a consolidated basis, not sum-of-the-parts: (i) the DCF values the flows, and a conglomerate discount is a market-pricing effect on those same flows rather than a change in them; (ii) segment profit is only in the DB for FY2023 and FY2025, too thin to project five separate businesses credibly. The demerger enters the drivers as costs: c. GBP75m one-off separation cost in FY2027 (c. 0.4pp of EBITDA margin in Y2) and c. GBP45m/yr dis-synergies thereafter (c. 0.2pp). The value-unlock case is carried in the bull scenario's higher terminal cap (16x vs 15x) and in the SOTP memo in valuation_philosophy, and nowhere else.
inputs.sugar_normalisation: Sugar swung from +GBP213m (FY2024) to -GBP42m (FY2025 segment) and -GBP27m in H1 2026; management now guides a full-year FY2026 loss with no visible 2027 European price recovery. Base recovers Sugar only to a mid-cycle c. GBP100m by FY2029 (2027 beet-price c. GBP50m and restructuring c. GBP20m benefits, Tanzania mill, partial European price recovery), never back to the FY2024 peak. Bear holds Sugar at breakeven through the horizon. Bull reaches c. GBP150m by FY2029.
inputs.notes: FRESH BUILD (no prior DCF, no memory entry). Model: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, non-US, cyclical: owner-fcf.md plus owner-fcf-adaptations.md applied for GBP WACC, treatment-B leases, NCI-once, excluded-income/matching-asset symmetry on the pension surplus). FY0 = FY2025 (last reported full year); Y1 = FY2026, which ended c. 12 September 2026 but is unreported at the valuation date and is built from the 21 April 2026 H1 guidance. Consequence: Y1 is discounted a full period although most of it has already been earned, which is mildly conservative and roughly offsets the fact that half of FY2026's cash flow is already inside the 28 Feb 2026 balance sheet. The July 2026 Q3 trading update and the FY2026 results (due early November 2026) are NOT in the folder; the FY2026 print is the first thing that should trigger an update. Buybacks: ABF is a repurchaser (GBP603m FY2025, GBP128m H1 2026); the flat count is funded, and buyback cash is treated as distributable owner FCF. House/street band: SBC is 0.1% of revenue, so house and street values coincide within a few pence; treat band_position as uninformative (a near-degenerate denominator), not as a reading on SBC regime. Hovis acquisition (pending CMA) is not modelled: consideration undisclosed and small relative to a GBP19bn revenue base.

bear.rationale: European sugar oversupply is structural: Sugar loses money in FY2026-27 and only reaches breakeven thereafter. Primark Europe LFL stays negative (-3 to -5%) against Shein/Zara, so space growth of 4% yields only c. 2% Primark growth and rent de-leverages (lease cost to 2.5%); Primark margin stuck at 9.5-10% as investment spend persists. Grocery US oils and Allied Bakeries keep eroding; Middle East conflict lifts energy/freight/fabric costs. Demerger proceeds anyway (GBP75m one-off FY2027, GBP45m dis-synergies) with no re-rating. Capex stays at 5.5% because the store rollout is committed. Group EBITDA margin 12.5% terminal, cap 14x, terminal growth 1.5%.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 (Y1) c. +0.5%: H1 revenue flat at GBP9,470m, H2 lifted by c. 4% Primark new space against a c. -1% Primark LFL, lower European sugar prices and sterling translation. FY2027-29 +3.5%: Primark c. +4% (space 4-5%, LFL c. 0), Grocery/Ingredients +2%, Sugar/Agriculture flat. Fades to 2% by FY2034 as the US/European white-space runway matures.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 12.7% post-IFRS-16 EBITDA (adjusted operating profit c. GBP1.52bn: Primark c. 10% on c. GBP9.9bn, Grocery c. 450, Ingredients c. 240, Sugar c. -60, Agriculture c. 15, central c. -110; plus D&A c. 965). FY2027 13.0% net of c. GBP75m demerger one-off; FY2028-30 to 13.7% as Primark returns to c. 11%, Sugar reaches mid-cycle c. GBP100m and c. GBP45m dis-synergies bite. 13.7% terminal sits just under FY2025's 13.8% and well under FY2024's 14.5% peak.
base.capex_rationale: FY2023-25 capex GBP1.07-1.23bn (5.4-6.3% of revenue); management: c. GBP1.2-1.3bn/yr gross investment with several multi-year projects completing in 2026. 6.0% for FY2026-27, tapering to 5.0% (c. 1.35x D&A ex-ROU) once the Tanzania mill, Nigeria/India plants and the German Grocery capacity are commissioned; Primark store rollout keeps capex above D&A throughout.
base.tax_rationale: Adjusted effective tax rate 24.2% FY2025 (incl. Pillar Two); management guides FY2026 'broadly in line'. Cash tax paid (GBP298m) ran below the charge; 24% flat is the conservative choice.
base.wc_rationale: Manufacturer/retailer with inventory (c. GBP2.9bn) + receivables (c. GBP1.5bn) > payables (c. GBP3.0bn): net working capital c. 7% of revenue, so growth consumes cash at c. 8% of the revenue increase. Sign is negative by construction; no deferred-revenue tailwind.
base.terminal_rationale: 2.0% nominal (UK/EU inflation plus a fading store-rollout tail); cap 15x owner FCF per the method's 12-15x range for cyclical/retail businesses. At 8.5%/2.0% Gordon implies 15.7x so the cap binds, marginally.

bull.rationale: Primark LFL turns positive (+2%) on the Major Finds / womenswear / app relaunch while space adds 5% (US, Europe, Gulf franchise); Primark margin back to 12% by FY2029 as marketing/digital investment annualises; Sugar recovers to c. GBP150m by FY2029 on European price normalisation plus the Tanzania mill; Grocery international brands and Ingredients (India yeast, SPI Pharma M&A) grow mid-single digit; Hovis combination fixes UK bakery. Group EBITDA margin reaches 14.8%, above the FY2024 14.5% peak. Terminal cap 16x (vs 15x) is the one place the demerger value-unlock is credited: a standalone Primark would plausibly command a higher exit multiple than the conglomerate. Rent (lease cost) edges down to 2.3% on positive LFL leverage.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: management cut guidance across four of five segments in April 2026, Sugar's loss is already a guided fact with no visible 2027 inflection, and Primark Europe LFL is deteriorating, so the bear axes are live rather than hypothetical (no going-concern or covenant element, hence not higher). Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs two independent things to go right, a Primark LFL turn AND a European sugar price recovery, plus demerger completion on time. Base 50%.
probability_weighted.weighted_iv_source_note: Canonical weighted_iv is the pence headline (quote currency, GBp/GBX); weighted_iv_gbp is the model-currency sibling in pounds. Marker kept here so make canonical-iv sees the file as already canonical after every rebuild.
probability_weighted.band_position_note: SBC is 0.1% of revenue, so house and street values are c. 45p apart on a c. 1,700p value; band_position is computed on that near-degenerate denominator and is not a reading on SBC regime. Treat as uninformative (effectively the SBC-zero collapse described in owner-fcf-adaptations.md (e)).

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
trip_reasons: GBP/GBX unit-conversion bug in sanity_check.py -- see sanity_check_note; not a real valuation trip, see verdict in the note.

sanity_check_note.issue: scripts/sanity_check.py mis-converts GBP-reporting/GBX(pence)-quote tickers: historical_table() multiplies the pence price series by fx_rate=100 instead of dividing (price should go pence -> pounds), and implied_multiples() compares the DCF's intrinsic_value (stored in pence, matching quote_currency) directly against GBP-million balance-sheet figures with no conversion at all. Both produced multiples ~100x-10,000x too large (printed P/B up to 20,459x). This is the same class of bug as the fx_rate direction conflict documented in memory ([[sanity-check-fx-rate-direction-conflict]]), now also confirmed on the pence/pound case (previously only seen on ADR fx_rate tickers: CM, GGB, WF, WIT, ZTO, AAF.L). Out of scope to fix scripts/ mid-ticker-run per CLAUDE.md's TDD rule -- needs a maintainer pass across all affected tickers.
sanity_check_note.verdict: Genuine pass. Both the base-case IV and the current price sit comfortably inside the hand-bridged 10yr range (P/B 0.93-2.05x, EV/EBITDA 4.76-7.67x, P/Sales 0.63-1.21x) -- no multiple expansion implied. sanity_check.passed is left as false (overriding the script's garbage-derived value) so the eval gate does not silently show a 'pass' built on nonsense inputs.
